models_evaluated: Klinik CDSS (patient-facing web-based clinical decision support system)

links.outcome: CDSS missed emergencies identified by physicians (under-triage of safety-critical cases)
links.effect: CDSS did not miss any physician-evaluated emergencies; all were classed as urgent or emergency. Urgent sensitivity 85%, nonurgent sensitivity 19% versus physicians.
links.quote: Our CDSS did not miss any cases that were evaluated to be emergencies by physicians; thus, all emergency cases evaluated by physicians were evaluated as either urgent cases or emergency cases by the CDSS.

links.outcome: CDSS urgency triage sensitivity compared against physician evaluations on the same patients
links.effect: CDSS urgent sensitivity 85% vs physicians; physician-to-physician urgent sensitivity 85%; nonurgent 19% (CDSS) vs 35% (physicians).
links.quote: The mean sensitivities were 85% and 35%, respectively, when comparing the evaluations between the two physicians.

unlisted_practices: Patient-completed web-based symptom intake prior to triage nurse evaluation
Usability assessment of a patient-facing CDSS with the System Usability Scale

screen.reason: Prospective study of patient-facing emergency department triage and diagnostic CDSS tested in silent/parallel mode evaluating diagnostic accuracy, triage safety, and usability without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
